Ukrainian Defense Forces have closed the Black Sea to Russian grain exports. Russia has acknowledged that the Black Sea route has been paralyzed following a series of Ukrainian attacks and is considering exporting grain via the Northern Sea Route. However, experts doubt this route can compensate for the loss of Black Sea capacity. Deputy Minister of Agriculture of the Russian Federation Maxim Borovoy announced that the possibility of using the Arctic route is being considered, according to the Russian social network for farmers, Agrobook.

According to him, the Northern Sea Route was previously hardly considered as a route for grain exports, but now the situation has changed.

# Türkiye Summons Ukraine Envoy Over Black Sea Attacks on Turkish Vessels

Ankara warns Kyiv over attacks on civilian shipping as the Russia-Ukraine war increasingly threatens commercial navigation in the Black Sea

![The rusting hull of the cargo ship Turgut S lies partially submerged in the shallow waters of Musura Bay, near the Black Sea port of Sulina, on May 10, 2026. (AFP)](https://d2wqffb2bc8st5.cloudfront.net/images/1788026981_kurdistan24.jpg)

**ERBIL (Kurdistan24) —** Türkiye summoned Ukraine’s ambassador on Saturday over attacks this week on a Turkish-operated vessel and a second ship that was sent to tow it in the Black Sea, as Ankara stepped up warnings that the Russia-Ukraine war is endangering civilian shipping and maritime security.

The Turkish Foreign Ministry said the attacks took place on Wednesday and Thursday, with the container ship Lider Bordo Mavi struck while sailing off Russia’s Black Sea coast on Wednesday.

The following day, the Lider Kocatepe, which had been dispatched to tow the damaged vessel, was also targeted.

The ministry did not provide details on whether anyone was injured or killed in either incident.

During a meeting with Ukraine’s ambassador, Turkish officials stressed the “absolute need” to protect people, property, navigation and the marine environment in the Black Sea, according to the ministry.

# Trivium China Weekly Recap | Washington’s China Policy: All Bluster, No Substance

[Andrew Polk](https://substack.com/@andrewpolk1)

More bark than bite, more rattle than snake, more smoke than fire – pick your idiom of choice, but what’s clear is that Washington has spent the past month making a great deal of noise about China while doing very little about it.

**This week’s US sanctions are the perfect example:** On August 20, President Donald Trump’s warned of “TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences” for any country that provides “any type of lifeline to Iran.”

**Days later, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled “Operation Economic Outcast,” Washington’s plan to cut Iran off from external economic support.**

· Bessent announced sanctions on more than 60 entities – including several in mainland China and Hong Kong – accused of supporting Iran’s nuclear and missile programs, cyber operations, and oil-revenue generation.

· He also warned that entities failing to cut ties with Iran risked being frozen out of the dollar-based financial system entirely.

**Notably absent from the list, however, were any Chinese oil refineries or banks.**

· That’s a telling gap, given these are the institutions facilitating the vast majority of Iran’s oil exports.

Hardly the TREMENDOUS consequences we were expecting.
